examples.name: rel_prereq_consistent
examples.note: EPR (--allow-relations): real MIT Course 6 prerequisite chain + transitivity + irreflexivity. FP control. Expect 0 contradictions, transitive prereq entailed (6.100A required by 6.5060).

examples.name: rel_prereq_broken
examples.note: EPR (--allow-relations): same MIT chain + one planted edge '6.100A requires 6.5060' -> a prerequisite cycle. Expect 1 contradiction (cycle DERIVED via transitivity + irreflexivity); minimal set is the cycle edges only (off-cycle edges excluded). Note states no conclusion, so the contradiction must be derived.

examples.name: rel_sports_fp_control
examples.note: EPR boundary/FP control (--allow-relations): A beat B, B beat C, C beat A, with NO transitivity axiom stated. Expect 0 contradictions -- the reasoner must NOT invent a cycle without a transitivity premise.

examples.name: rel_command_tree
examples.note: EPR theory-TREE (--allow-relations): a chain-of-command ladder (Atlas>Brava>Cruz>Diaz>Estes) + command transitivity + a command->outrank bridge + rank asymmetry. Unlike the cycle fixtures this is tree-SHAPED: each derived claim builds on the previous theorem (Atlas commands Cruz -> Atlas commands Diaz -> Atlas commands Estes -> Atlas outranks Estes), a depth-4 relational ladder, then a relational REDUCTIO ('suppose Estes outranks Atlas' -> refuted via the derived outranking + asymmetry). Expect 0 contradictions, a layered tree, and 1 refuted supposition.

examples.name: rel_authority_conflict
examples.note: EPR HIDDEN inconsistency, no planted cycle (--allow-relations): each premise is fine alone, but the relational derivation surfaces a conflict -- 'Atlas governs Diaz' (transitive over Atlas>Brava>Cruz>Diaz) + 'governing implies accountability' bridge entails 'Atlas is accountable for Diaz', which contradicts the axiom 'Atlas is not accountable for Diaz'. The negative axiom targets Atlas SPECIFICALLY (reachable only through all 3 hops), so the minimal inconsistent set is the WHOLE ladder (3 governance edges + transitivity + bridge + the negative axiom): the inconsistency is reachable only through multi-step relational reasoning, not a single bridge step.

examples.name: rel_two_branch_conflict
examples.note: EPR TWO-BRANCH inconsistency (--allow-relations): NEITHER contradicting conclusion is a stated axiom -- both are DERIVED deep in two separate chains that collide. Branch A: Atlas>Brava>Cruz>Diaz allies-chain + ally-transitivity + 'ally implies trust' bridge entails 'Atlas trusts Diaz'. Branch B: Atlas>Echo>Felix>Diaz rivals-chain + rival-transitivity + 'rival implies NOT trust' bridge entails 'Atlas does not trust Diaz'. The two derived theorems are direct negations, so the minimal inconsistent set spans BOTH full branches (all 6 edges + both transitivity rules + both bridges). Proves the axiom set inconsistent purely because deep two-sided derivation produces P and not-P; rendered as a flat minimal set (no consistent theory to grow a tree from).
